import { Steps, Aside } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import SkillTable from '../../../../components/SkillTable.astro';

## After generating

Generation copied each `apps/*/.env.example` to `.env`, ran `yarn install`,
formatted the code and made the first commit.

<Steps>

1. **Run the API** (a [nest-api](../../nest-api/development/) on port 5000).
   Its trusted origins and CORS must include every app you run.

2. **Start every app:**

   ```sh
   yarn dev   # turbo runs each app's dev server
   ```

   landing on 3000, auth on 3001, client on 3002, admin on 3003 (those you
   generated).

3. **Sign in:** open the client at `http://localhost:3002`. You're sent to the
   auth app's `/login`, and after signing in, back to the client.

</Steps>

<Aside type="caution" title="Sharing the session locally">
On `localhost`, every app is the same host on a different port, so they share
cookies without a cookie domain: leave the API's `BETTER_AUTH_COOKIE_DOMAIN`
empty (the default). To mirror production's subdomains instead, use
`*.lvh.me` (which resolves to `127.0.0.1`): `http://app.lvh.me:3002`,
`http://auth.lvh.me:3001` and so on, set the API's cookie domain to `.lvh.me`,
list those hostnames in each app's `VITE_APP_ALLOWED_HOSTS`, and update the
`VITE_APP_*_HOST` values and the API's origins to match.
</Aside>

## Scripts

Root scripts run across every workspace through Turborepo:

| Script | Does |
|---|---|
| `yarn dev` | Every app's dev server |
| `yarn build` | Typecheck and build every app |
| `yarn typecheck`, `yarn lint` | Across apps and packages |
| `yarn format`, `yarn format:check` | Prettier |
| `yarn secrets [-e env]` | Each workspace's `.env` from Infisical |

One app: `yarn workspace client dev`, `yarn workspace landing build`.

## API types

`@scope/types` needs `packages/types/.env` (not created for you):

```ini
API_DOC_URL=http://localhost:5000/openapi-json
API_DOC_USER=admin       # the API's BASIC_AUTH_USER
API_DOC_PASSWORD=…       # the API's BASIC_AUTH_PASS
```

Then `yarn workspace @scope/types gen`, and commit `src/types/api/`: every app
compiles against it. A fresh project ships empty placeholders so it typechecks
before the API exists.

## Adding a page

The project's own [task skills](#building-with-claude-code) carry the full steps for each of these.

Add the route to the app's `src/app/router.tsx`, and to `src/app/nav.tsx` if it
belongs in the sidebar (the shell builds the sidebar from that list, not from
the router). Put its data calls in `src/features/<name>/api.ts` with
`baseApi.injectEndpoints`.

## Adding a package

Create `packages/<name>` with a `package.json` named `@scope/<name>` whose
`exports` points at `./src/index.ts`, depend on it from the apps
(`"@scope/<name>": "workspace:*"`), and add a line for it to the Dockerfile's
dependency stage. If it contains Tailwind classes, add it to the `@source` lines
in the UI kit's `globals.css`.

## Building with Claude Code

The project ships its own guidance for Claude Code, generated with it and
stripped to the features it has:

- **`CLAUDE.md`** at the root: the monorepo's commands, which app does what, and the rules (shared code is a package, one `baseApi`, sign-in on the auth app's origin, `VITE_*` per app). Claude Code loads it in every session
  in the project.
- **Task skills** in `.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`: step-by-step recipes
  that point at the template's own example code. Ask for the task in plain
  words ("add an endpoint for invoices") and the matching skill loads.

<SkillTable template="react-monorepo" />

A skill that belongs to a feature arrives with it: adding the feature later
with [`stack add`](../../../reference/cli/#stack-add) brings its skill and its
`CLAUDE.md` sections too. Both are yours to edit as the project grows its own
conventions. See [Building with Claude Code](../../../guides/claude-code/) for
the whole workflow, from a design to a backlog.
